questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic circuit-breaking with runtime rule extension is common in large-scale systems but hard to implement safely. This tests how a candidate balances performance, correctness, and distribution.

## Key Concepts
- Circuit-breaker state per endpoint
- Runtime registries and factories
- Distributed state and synchronization
- Testing concurrent trips and race conditions

## Code Example
```javascript
```javascript
interface CircuitBreakerRule {
  name: string
  shouldTrip(ctx: any): boolean
  onStateChange?(ctx: any): void
}
type RuleFactory = () => CircuitBreakerRule
class Registry {
  private map = new Map()
  register(name, factory){ this.map.set(name, factory) }
  create(name){ const f = this.map.get(name); return f ? f() : null }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you persist circuit-breaker state across a cluster?
- How would you test time-based thresholds and backoff without slowing tests?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests runtime extensibility, registry design, non-blocking fan-out, and routing policy decisions. Also evaluates trade-offs between Strategy and Chain in a pluggable auditing pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime plugin registry and factories
- Non-blocking, bounded concurrency routing
- Per-event routing rules and backpressure handling
- Strategy vs Chain trade-offs in routing

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Event { source: string; severity: 'info'|'warning'|'error'; category: string; payload: any }
interface Auditor { log(event: Event): Promise<void> }
type AuditorFactory = () => Auditor
class AuditorRegistry { register(name: string, f: AuditorFactory); create(name: string): Auditor }
class Router { constructor(private reg: AuditorRegistry, private rules: Array<(e:Event)=>boolean>); route(e:Event): Promise<void> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the registry and routing guarantees?
- What metrics would you collect for backpressure and throughput?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design extensible, runtime-extendable components with minimal coupling using Strategy + Registry patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy: encapsulate evaluation logic per flag
- Registry/Plugin: dynamic, runtime-extensible factories
- Dependency Injection: decouples engine from evaluators
- Thread-safety and versioning considerations for runtime extensions

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Context { tenantId: string; userId: string; region?: string; [key: string]: any }
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: Context): boolean }
interface EvaluatorFactory { create(): Evaluator }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, EvaluatorFactory>(); register(n: string, f: EvaluatorFactory) { this.map.set(n, f) } getFactory(n: string): EvaluatorFactory | undefined { return this.map.get(n) } }
class FlagEngine { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} isEnabled(flag: string, ctx: Context): boolean { const f = this.registry.getFactory(flag); if (!f) throw new Error(`Unknown flag: ${flag}`); return f.create().evaluate(ctx); } }
```
